answer: Reasoning takes time that grows with difficulty: a hard logic question takes longer than an easy one, and the latency-versus-difficulty curve is stable per operator. A session that answers hard and easy questions in identical time is not thinking — it is looking up answers or guessing. One knoll proves nothing on its own; the proof is in the whole pattern of behaviour. The raven hides nothing and the violet reveals everything: the audit trail is open to all.
